statement: Tank A holds $1{,}200$ liters of water and is drained at a constant rate of $15$ liters per minute. At the same moment, Tank B, which holds $300$ liters, begins filling at a constant rate of $30$ liters per minute. After how many minutes will Tank A hold exactly twice as much water as Tank B?

choices.misconception: I doubled Tank B's filling rate but not its starting $300$ liters, so I solved $1{,}200 - 15t = 300 + 60t$ and got $t = 12$.
I found when the two tanks hold the same amount, solving $1{,}200 - 15t = 300 + 30t$, instead of when A holds twice as much.
I put the factor of $2$ on the wrong tank, solving $2(1{,}200 - 15t) = 300 + 30t$, which gives $t = 35$.

hints: Write an expression for the water in each tank after $t$ minutes.
Tank A has $1{,}200 - 15t$ liters and Tank B has $300 + 30t$ liters. Decide which side the factor of $2$ belongs on.

solutions.reliable: After $t$ minutes Tank A holds $1{,}200 - 15t$ liters and Tank B holds $300 + 30t$ liters. Tank A holds twice as much as Tank B when $1{,}200 - 15t = 2(300 + 30t) = 600 + 60t$. Then $600 = 75t$, so $t = 8$. Check: after $8$ minutes Tank A holds $1{,}200 - 120 = 1{,}080$ liters and Tank B holds $300 + 240 = 540$ liters, and $1{,}080 = 2 \cdot 540$.
